question.prompt: What are the sum and product, respectively, of the two roots of \(x²-5x+6=0\)? (Answer in order, separated by a comma.)

solutions.explanation: \(a=1\), \(b=-5\), and \(c=6\). The sum of the two roots is \(-b/a=5\), and their product is \(c/a=6\). (This can also be verified by directly finding the roots \(2\) and \(3\).)
solutions.title: Read the sum and product from the coefficients

solutions.explanation:
Factoring finds the roots themselves:
\[
x^2-5x+6=(x-2)(x-3).
\]
The product is zero exactly when \(x=2\) or \(x=3\). Their sum and product, in the requested order, are \(2+3=5\) and \(2\cdot3=6\).
solutions.title: Find the roots by factoring
